question.leadin: In 1962, this man was imprisoned for life at Robben Island.
question.text: Name this civil rights leader who became the first black president of South Africa.
question.clue: This man evaded capture by police by pretending to be a cook and gardener on Liliesleaf Farm, which later led to his imprisonment with 19 others in what became known as the Rivonia Trial.

swap.text: Osama bin Laden first appeared on the FBI's Most Wanted Terrorists list after his involvement in an 1998 embassy bombing in this country with capital at Nairobi.
swap.clue: This country's first pro-American post-colonial government was heavily criticized by opposition leader and former Vice President Jaramogi Oginga Odinga, the founder of its People's Union.

question.leadin: This country shares Lake Turkana with Ethiopia and the Kibera slum is in its capital city of Nairobi. --.
question.text: Name this East African country north of Tanzania.
question.clue: The Kapenguria Six were arrested during a conflict in this modern-day country, which also saw the British construct "protected villages" to detain civilians.

swap.leadin: The Islamic Courts Union once controlled much of the southern part of this country, but in 2006 it splintered into groups like al-Shabaab.
swap.text: Name this country on the Horn of Africa. It has been considered a failed state for its inability to control a civil war in its territory or piracy in its waters.
swap.clue: After the dictator Siad Barre was ousted from power in this nation, warlords began to take control of autonomous regions such as Puntland.

question.text: The Moroccan explorer Leo Africanus wrote of the fabulous wealth of this Malian city, while Europeans often considered it to be a fantastical, faraway location.
question.clue: The Frenchman Rene Caillie was the first European to return alive from visiting this city.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about this largest African country.
swap.text: This North African country is home to the Ottoman citadel of Santa Cruz in its city of Oran.
swap.clue: This country was the home to the Movement for the Triumph of Democratic Liberties, and its later independence activists included Houari Boumedienne and Ahmed Ben Bella.

question.leadin: This leader's secret police, the State Research Bureau, entrapped dissidents through women planted in public spaces.
question.text: Identify this leader, whose construction of a National Mosque was delayed by his administration's rampant embezzlement. This successor of Milton Obote expelled all Asians from his country.
question.clue: This man awarded himself the 'Victorious Cross', a law doctorate, and the title 'Conqueror of the British Empire', as well as 'Lord of all the Beasts of the Earth'.

swap.leadin: This empire secured power after defeating the Denkyira kingdom made up of the Akan people.
swap.text: Name this empire ruled by figures such as King Osei Tutu, whose capital was located at the city of Kumasi.
swap.clue: This empire was split off from the Denkyira Empire by its founder Osei Tutu.

question.leadin: The Underground Railroad wasn't a disaster, but answer these questions about incidents what were.
question.text: In this African country, 192 people were killed and at least 160 more injured in a June 2002 accident at Moamba.
question.clue: A right-wing organization opposing the socialist government of this country drew support from such cities as the Beira port in Sofala province, was formed by Andre Matsangaissa, and laid down its arms in the 1990s following the Rome Accords.

swap.text: Ghana's salt trade was inherited by the Sosso empire, whose king Sumunguru ("soo-muhn-GOO-roo") was defeated by this ruler with a poisoned arrow. An oral epic named for this ruler relates how he became the first Mansa of the Mali empire.
swap.answerHtml: Sundiata Keita [or Sunjata; or Sonjara; or Manding Diara; or Sogolon Djata; or Nare Maghan; or Sogo Sogo Simbon Salaba; prompt on Keita]
swap.clue: She gave birth to a sickly child, a child whose entire family, including his eleven brothers, was killed by an invading Kaniaga ruler, though Sumanguru left this child alive because he thought this boy would die soon enough.

question.text: Much of the unhappiness of Mozambique was centered in this city, the nation's capital.

swap.text: One ruler sent an "International Association" of this region in place of his country Belgium. The dismemberment of workers' hands in this region is recounted in Adam Hochschild's book King Leopold's Ghost.
swap.answerHtml: Congo [or Congo Basin or Congo Free State; accept Democratic Republic of the Congo; accept Belgian Congo; accept Republic of the Congo; prompt on Zaire]
swap.clue: The first conflict with this name involved the overthrow of Mobutu Sese-Seko, who renamed a country with this name to Zaire .

question.text: The Coptic Patriarch of Alexandria chose the head of this kingdom's Tewahedo Church before a 9th-century schism. Kaleb and Ezana were Christian neguses of this kingdom based in modern-day Eritrea and Ethiopia.
question.answerHtml: Aksum [or Kingdom of Axum or Aksumite Empire or Mängəśtä ʾäksum; prompt on Abyssinia]
question.clue: The Zagwe ("ZAHG-way") dynasty replaced this kingdom, whose rulers spoke Ge'ez ("gee-EZ").

swap.leadin: In 1960 under the backing of Belgian mining companies, the State of Katanga under Moise Tshombe declared independence from this leader's government.
swap.text: Name this first Prime Minister of an independent Democratic Republic of the Congo. This leader was deposed by Mobutu Sese Seko after seeking assistance from the Soviet Union.
swap.clue: His time in office saw the rise of secessionist movement under Moise Tshombe of the CONAKAT party, leading to UN intervention.

question.text: This name was held by a Malagasy queen who reigned for 30 years and persecuted Christians, though her successor of the same name christianized Madagascar. The final queen of this name died in exile in Reunion.
question.clue: The son of a ruler with this regnal name attempted to undermine their authority by agreeing to the Lambert Charter.

swap.leadin: Prior to the American Revolution, Richard Oswald rebuilt an abandoned trading fort on Bunce Island in what would become this country, leading thousands of residents to be shipped to the American Southeast.
swap.text: Name this country where Thomas Peters, a Black Loyalist, moved with three dozen Amistad mutineers after leaving Nova Scotia.
swap.clue: This country used IMF funds to pay South African mercenary firm Executive Outcomes to terrorize its citizens.

question.text: This Zulu chief who would eventually be succeeded by his half-brother Mpande, killed Retief's band of settlers, thus escalating the conflict with the Boer settlers.

swap.text: The Alaouite or Sherifian Dynasty consolidated its power in 1659 when Mulay R-Rshid conquered this Moroccan city, which experienced its greatest period under the reign of Yaqub al-Mansur.
swap.clue: This city, where the building of the El Badi palace was funded by ransom money demanded from the Portuguese after its rulers' victory at the Battle of Alcacer Quibir [al-KAH-ser KEE-beer].

question.text: This queen mother of Ejisu led the Ashanti in the War of the Golden Stool against the British imperial government, after refusing to turn over the stool to Frederick Hodgson. She died in exile in the Seychelles.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a Berber dynasty, FTPE.
swap.text: They originated in Mauritania, but after a period of expansion in the 11th Century, they built the city of Marrakech and based themselves in Morocco.
swap.clue: Guided by the preaching of Waggag ibn Zallu and Ibn Yasin, this dynasty expanded to take Kumbi Saleh, fought Portugal at Ourique, and defended al-Andalus from Alfonso the Brave at Sagrajas.
